newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AGL sees energy market shakeup.
newsitem.headline: AGL sees energy market shakeup.

text.p: Australian Gas Light Co (AGL) said on Monday it expected Australia's energy market would see a significant rationalisation in the number of players within the next five years

"There are about 25 to 30 energy companies in the market now. In the next five to 10 years, I see that moving down to about 10," AGL managing director and chief executive Len Bleasel told a Institute for International Research energy conference.
Bleasel said the rationalisation should not be a concern if regulations were in place which ensured a level playing field for all participants.
Bleasel said as long as Australian states continued to set their own regulations then there would not be a level playing field for the energy market in Australia.
"Every state is going to ensure its interests are looked after. We still have a very fragmented approach right across the country," Bleasel said.
The most important factor to free up the market was to bring about producer competition, Bleasel said.
"The best price for consumers will only come when we all (producers and distributors) compete," he said.
It was important that Australian companies could grow in stature in order to compete in the international market place.

"Market dominance in Australia should not be measured without consideration of the size of the worldwide energy companies who are now buying businesses in our energy market," Bleasel said, adding that controls on the energy industry should be simple and unduplicated, to have "one set of rules across the entire country."
An appeal process must be an intrinsic right in any dealings between parties to ensure the regulator was held accountable for its decisions, Bleasel said.
